items.readable_text:
Content:
When simplifying numerical expressions, it is generally preferable to avoid having radicals in the denominator. In cases where we wish to remove a radical from a denominator, we must rationalize the denominator.

Content:
If the denominator of an expression consists of two terms and includes one or more radicals, we rationalize it by multiplying both the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the denominator.

Content:
To illustrate, consider the following expression:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{1+\sqrt{2}}]

Content:
To find the conjugate of the denominator [MATH: 1+\sqrt{2},] we flip the sign between the two terms. So, the conjugate of the denominator is

Content:
[MATH: 1\,{\color{blue}{-}}\,\sqrt{2}.]

Content:
Now, to rationalize the denominator, we start by multiplying both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate [MATH: 1-\sqrt{2},] as follows:

Content:
[MATH: (1)/(1 + sqrt(2))|=; (1)/(1 + sqrt(2)) ⋅ (1 − sqrt(2))/(1 − sqrt(2))|=; (1 ⋅ (1 − sqrt(2)))/((1 + sqrt(2))(1 − sqrt(2)))|=; (1 − sqrt(2))/((1 + sqrt(2))(1 − sqrt(2)))|=]

Content:
Now, we recall the difference of squares formula:

Content:
[MATH: (a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2]

Content:
Applying the difference of squares formula with [MATH: a=1, b=\sqrt 2] to simplify the denominator, we get

Content:
[MATH: (1 − sqrt(2))/((1 + sqrt(2))(1 − sqrt(2)))|=; (1 − sqrt(2))/(1^{2} − (sqrt(2))^{2})|=; (1 − sqrt(2))/(1 − 2)|=; (1 − sqrt(2))/(− 1)|=; sqrt(2) − 1.]

items.title: Rationalizing Denominators Containing Two Terms

sections.normalized_html:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is [MATH: \sqrt{3} + 1.]

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate [MATH: \sqrt{3} + 1,] and simplify:

[MATH: \eqalign{ \dfrac {2}{\sqrt{3} - 1} &= \[5pt] \dfrac {2}{\sqrt{3} - 1} \cdot \dfrac {\sqrt{3} + 1} {\sqrt{3} + 1} &= \[5pt] \dfrac {2\left(\sqrt 3 + 1\right)} {\left(\sqrt{3}\right)^2 - 1^2} &= \[5pt] \dfrac {2\left(\sqrt 3 + 1\right)} {3 - 1} &= \[5pt] \dfrac {2\left(\sqrt 3 + 1\right)} {2} &= \[5pt] \sqrt 3 + 1 & }]

Item 2 — Example: Rationalizing Denominators Containing Two Terms
